I've come back to this post several times and each time I wonder how to interpret it. Are you saying trans activists are rational in trying to deplatform anyone who believes in Blanchard's typology regardless of its truth?

I guess it depends on several factors. (A Drake equation for timeless genocide, if you will.)

  1. How likely Blanchardians are to persuade the general public they are right.

  2. How likely the general public is to take this as a negative.

  3. How likely a negative perception is to lead to anti-trans action.

  4. How severe the action would be.

Factor 2 is less obvious than one may assume without thinking. Consider the change in attitude towards homosexuality.
replies.author: Rat Analyst

replies.text: Whenever an autogynephilic transsexual I know has come out about being AGP and buying Blanchardianism, it has gone perfectly fine. I feel like people overestimate that Blanchardian/transphobia link due to confounding (anti-trans people know that Blanchardianism pisses trans people off, and so pick it up, leading to a correlation despite less causal influence of Blanchardianism on attitudes to trans people). It seems like it should be relevant to investigate empirically, but I haven't gotten around to it yet.

replies.text:
I'm saying that Emezi repeatedly states "the stakes are life and death" and seems to share the post's view that Adichie's <a href=https://www.facebook.com/chimamandaadichie/photos/a.469824145943.278768.40389960943/10154893542340944/?type=3&theater>incredibly general statements</a> are ultimately tantamount to genocide. Adichie also describes being transgender as a "way to be" that seems analogous to M's "I want you to exist". <a href=https://www.chimamanda.com/>This post</a> kicked off the latest round of the conflict. Doesn't seem to have anything to do with Blanchardianism specifically.

So I'm saying that some people seriously think they have solved the Drake equation and it's genocide. Adichie called JKR's essay "reasonable" and it alluded to a few policy suggestions, but I haven't seen Adichie make policy suggestions herself. So it really is like in the post where just expressing the beliefs is consequential and evil enough, according to Emezi.
